name: Guvar nu Shaak
subtitle: cluster beans cooked down with crushed peanut and sesame until the bitterness turns nutty

ingredients.note: pick young, flexible pods; woody ones stay bitter
guvar is heavy; ajwain settles it
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: String the beans properly: snap the tip and pull the fibre down each side. A single missed string ruins a mouthful.
Roast and crush the peanuts yourself and keep them coarse — powder disappears, coarse crush gives the dish its grain.
If the guvar is older and stringy, soak the cut pieces in warm salted water for 15 minutes before cooking.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a kadhai and crackle the mustard seeds, then add the ajwain and asafoetida.
Add the crushed garlic and green chilli and fry 1 minute until the garlic smells sweet.
Tip in the cut guvar and turn it through the oil for 3-4 minutes until the pods turn a brighter green.
Add the turmeric, chilli powder, coriander powder and salt and stir 30 seconds.
Pour in the water, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, stirring twice.
steps.tip: Low and covered. Guvar cooked hard on high stays squeaky in the middle however long you leave it.

steps.text: Check a pod — it should be tender enough to crush between finger and thumb with no snap. Give it 5 minutes more if not.
Uncover, add the crushed peanut, sesame and jaggery and cook 4-5 minutes until the water has gone and the beans are coated in a dry, nutty masala.
steps.tip: Add the peanuts late. Boiled peanuts go soft and lose the whole point of them.

steps.text: Take off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and coriander, and serve with rotli and dal-bhaat.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated. Reheat in a dry pan over medium heat, no water — this shaak is meant to be dry and water makes it sludgy.
